messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release `v2.4.1` -> eu-west-1 (canary id: cb-324000). 50% traffic. Hold window 20m. Monitoring hooks: `canary/cpu`, `canary/latency_p50_p95`, `canary/error_rate`. Alert @david-oncall @mia-sre if any threshold trips.

alice: ack — watching dashboards (grafana: /d/edge/canary-v2). will call out anomalies. :eyes:

ben-platform: quick heads-up, support needs a short statuspage + email snippet ready in case we pin/rollback. drafting now, ping if wording needs change.

carla-support: thanks @ben-platform. for dedicated customers do we call out explicit pinning to previous runtime or just say "temporary rollout pause"? also SLA impact?

david-oncall: set concrete triggers: if `error_rate` > 0.5% for 5m OR p95 latency increases by +300ms sustained for 5m -> initiate pin/rollback. If triggered, oncall will run pin script and notify support to publish. SLA not automatically changed; we escalate to ops for SLA exceptions.

alice: +1 to triggers. also add immediate hold if any 5xx surge from model-server logs (>=3/min for 3min).

ben-platform: statuspage snippet draft (short):
```
Component: Redwood API (eu-west-1)
Status: Degraded Performance (investigating)
Summary: A canary rollout for release v2.4.1 is under investigation due to elevated latency for a subset of requests. We may pause the rollout or pin traffic back to the previous version while we investigate.
Impact: Some requests served from eu-west-1 may see higher latency or transient errors. Dedicated customers are unaffected unless we perform an explicit capacity change and will be notified separately.
ETA: updates in ~30 minutes or as we have new information.
```

ben-platform: customer email draft:
Subject: Notice: temporary rollout in eu-west-1 — potential higher latency
Body:
"Hi — we're rolling out an update to our inference runtime in eu-west-1. We're seeing higher-than-expected latency for a subset of traffic and may pause the rollout or revert the change while we investigate. If your integration is impacted we'll follow up with targeted instructions. No immediate action required. — Redwood Inference Ops"

carla-support: looks good. suggest adding a one-liner for Dedicated: "Dedicated customers: we'll contact you directly if we need to pin your reserved capacity to a prior runtime."

mia-sre: one more ops note: prefer routing fallback to previous model variant before full rollback when possible. Steps: 1) update routing policy to prefer model:v2.3.9 2) pin traffic 3) collect traces for 15m. can we automate step 1 via deploy-bot?

ben-platform: yes — deploy-bot supports a `pin-traffic` action. initiating pause now and will run `pin-traffic --target v2.3.9 --regions eu-west-1` if triggers hit. leaving hold open until canary window closes or trigger occurs.

deploy-bot: ACTION: canary cb-324000 paused at 3240001280 by user request (ben-platform). job_id: jb-89c3. readiness: monitoring hooks still active. queued pin action: `pin-traffic --target v2.3.9 --region eu-west-1` (will run on trigger).

carla-support: I'll prepare the statuspage update and scheduled email to go out if pin runs. publishing plan: immediate statuspage update (short) now + targeted customer email queued for manual send once pin is confirmed. will post final copy once published.

ben-platform: final note — post-mortem owners: @alice (canary metrics), @mia-sre (runtime regression), @carla-support (customer comms). tagging here so we can triage after resolution.

carla-support: published statuspage snippet and queued email draft to the Ops queue. will send on confirmation. :white_check_mark:

(automated) deploy-bot: trigger check at 3240001456: no metric breach during paused window. canary remains paused. recommend manual resume or pin if further evidence emerges.

alice: noted — will keep monitoring for next 30m and post final recommendation in this thread."
